name: Rebuild CZ-style phase-distortion shapes with an external phase chain (skew, formant, sync, fold)
goal: Recreate Casio-like phase-distortion oscillator shapes in a modular/grid synth by driving a sine from an external phase ramp, then inserting skew, formant/PWM, fold+formant, and sync stages; animate the shape amount with an envelope for filterless brightness, and optionally raise a sync/frequency multiple for resonant overtones.

source.title: What is a Phase Distortion Oscillator and why is it

prerequisites: Modular or grid environment with phase oscillator, phase shaping (skew/bend, formant/PWM), sync, and scope
Familiarity with disabling an oscillator's internal phase and feeding 100% external phase

inputs.name: shape_stack
inputs.description: Ordered phase processors, e.g. [skew], [formant], [fold, formant-12st], [sync-12st, skew]

inputs.name: shape_mod
inputs.description: Envelope or LFO mapped to the primary shape amount

outputs.name: pd_voice
outputs.description: Sine-based PD voice with switchable/combinable shape modes

constraints: Portable signal-flow recipe for Web Audio / Traveler-inspired / any hybrid synth with comparable modules; not affiliated with any vendor.
Do not copy proprietary factory preset banks, wavetable file names, or sample packs; use original/free waves or generic shapes.
Steps and numeric values are grounded only in the YouTube Show-transcript text; approximate where the speaker gestured without stating a number.
Built-in 'Phase-1'-style feedback with near-zero delay may not be reproducible with a long delay; treat feedback as optional/product-specific.
Align phases (phase reset on note) before comparing shapes so offsets do not look like different algorithms.

steps.action: Start with a sine oscillator. Disable its internal phase (or set internal phase ratio to 0) and drive phase modulation from an external phaser/ramp at 100% so the sine returns.
steps.expect: Scope matches a normal sine; pitch tracks the phaser

steps.action: Saw-like PD: insert a skew/bend on the phase so the ramp races through the first half and stretches the second (knee around 50% amplitude). Invert polarity if needed to match a reference Phase-1 oscillator.
steps.expect: Opening skew morphs sine → saw-like without a filter

steps.action: PWM/formant-style: use a formant (or PWM) phase shaper so phase stays at the start, runs quickly through the cycle, then holds at the end until reset — classic pulse-width-like PD.
steps.expect: Scope shows dwell at ends; tone thins/thickens with amount

steps.action: Folded variant: fold the lower half of the wave upward, then apply formant/PWM; for a precise match the transcript uses about −12 semitones on the formant stage and order matters (formant before the other stage).
steps.expect: A distinct folded-then-squeezed sine family appears

steps.action: Sync+skew: put a sync stage at +12 st (double frequency) then skew to slide the doubled humps together — another CZ-like bright shape. Whole-number octave sync ratios (12 or 24 st) keep the effect tonal.
steps.expect: Brighter, more overtone-rich PD; skew still animates the shape

steps.action: Squeezed whole-wave: shift phase by about 25%, then move formant to squeeze the entire sine. Animate whichever shape control is primary with an ADSR (CZ historically used rich multi-stage envelopes on DCW).
steps.expect: Envelope on shape gives plucky filterless accents

steps.action: Resonant tilt: raise the oscillator's frequency/sync multiple (or dedicated F control akin to sync) while modulating shape so overtones bloom like resonance — related to but not identical to plain sync.
steps.expect: Shape motion still dominates; extra multiple adds resonant edge

verification: Each shape_stack setting matches a different sine deformation on the scope
Envelope on shape amount changes timbre without needing a filter
Pitch remains that of the external phaser/fundamental
